title: The Elves (Die Wichtelmänner)
summary: A poor, honest shoemaker had only leather left for a single pair of shoes. He cut the leather out in the evening, said his prayers, and went peacefully to sleep....
full_text:
A poor, honest shoemaker had only leather left for a single pair of shoes. He cut the leather out in the evening, said his prayers, and went peacefully to sleep.

In the morning, he found the shoes finished upon his workbench, stitched with such miraculous perfection that not a single stitch was awry! A customer bought them for double the price.

Night after night, the miracle continued: whatever leather he cut in the evening was finished by morning into magnificent footwear. The shoemaker became a prosperous man.

One night, the shoemaker and his wife hid behind a curtain to watch. At midnight, two tiny, naked little men slipped in, sat cross-legged, and stitched with lightning speed until dawn!

The grateful wife said: "These little men have made us rich; let us sew them tiny coats, shirts, breeches, and knit tiny shoes!"

On Christmas Eve, they laid the tiny clothes on the bench instead of leather. At midnight, the little elves arrived, dressed themselves in the fine coats, danced merrily upon the table, singing:
"Now we are boys so fine and neat,
Why should we longer cobble the street?"

They leaped out the window into the night. Though they never returned, good fortune and prosperity blessed the honest shoemaker to the end of his days.
moral: Unseen blessings reward honest labor; gratitude clothed in kindness blesses the helper.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Elves (Die Wichtelmänner)"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
